build_inputs.angles:
1. Twin turbo four litre V8, five hundred and ninety one horsepower, five hundred and ninety pound feet. Edmunds timed it to sixty in three point three seconds. This is a station wagon.

2. Audi sold an RS6 in America once before, back in 2003, and only as a sedan. The wagon was never offered here. Two generations came and went that Americans could not buy. This is the first RS6 Avant Audi ever sold in the United States.

3. It weighs nearly five thousand pounds and it still does three point three. Quattro all wheel drive means it just leaves, no drama, no wheelspin.

4. It is not an A6 with badges on it. The body is physically wider than the car it is based on, so almost nothing bolts over from a standard A6.

5. Eight speed automatic, and that is the only way it came. There has never been a manual C8 RS6, so nobody is hunting for one.

6. It will do the grocery run, fit the dog, take the kids, and then out drag almost anything at the lights. That is the entire argument for it.

Rules for this build:
- Content is about the C8 RS6 Avant generation, 2020 to 2023 pre facelift, not this one chassis.
- Do not say it was the first RS6 sold in America. The C5 sedan came here in 2003. It is the first RS6 Avant sold here.
- Power is 591 hp. Zero to sixty is 3.3 seconds tested by Edmunds, or 3.5 seconds as Audi claims. Do not mix the two in one sentence.
- Say nearly five thousand pounds, not an exact curb weight. Sources disagree.
- Do not give an exact count of how many came to the US.

title: Audi RS6 Avant - C8

history.fact: Audi first sold Americans the 591-horsepower wagon in 2020 after sending us only the C5 sedan in 2003 and skipping two generations.

scenes.headline: 11.4-Second Wagon

scenes.headline: First U.S. Avant
scenes.narration: Audi first sold Americans the 591-horsepower wagon in 2020 after sending us only the C5 sedan in 2003 and skipping two generations.

scenes.narration: Edmunds got to sixty in 3.3 seconds using launch control and quattro to put the power down through all four wheels.

scenes.headline: Hot-V Turbos
scenes.narration: Its twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 makes 590 pound-feet and keeps the exhaust path short by tucking both turbos between the cylinder banks.

scenes.headline: RS Mode
scenes.narration: The RS button on the wheel brings up your own settings for the suspension and the eight-speed automatic.

scenes.headline: $110K → $100K
scenes.narration: They started at about $110,000 new and they go for about $100,000 today, so would you daily this wagon or buy a sports car?

script: This station wagon ran the quarter mile in 11.4 seconds at nearly 5,000 pounds. Audi first sold Americans the 591-horsepower wagon in 2020 after sending us only the C5 sedan in 2003 and skipping two generations. Those headlights? Edmunds got to sixty in 3.3 seconds using launch control and quattro to put the power down through all four wheels. Audi widened the body instead of rebadging the A6 Avant, but the tailgate is one of the few panels they still share. Its twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 makes 590 pound-feet and keeps the exhaust path short by tucking both turbos between the cylinder banks. The RS button on the wheel brings up your own settings for the suspension and the eight-speed automatic. They started at about $110,000 new and they go for about $100,000 today, so would you daily this wagon or buy a sports car?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2021 Audi RS6 Avant, finished in Nardo Gray with a black interior. The odometer on this RS6 currently displays approximately 23,700 miles. This Audi is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report, and it shows this wagon has reportedly been registered to one owner in California since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes the Executive, Black Optic, and Driver Assistance packages, and 22-inch wheels. Notable modifications reported by the seller include an Alcantara-trimmed steering wheel, Auto Parking and Auto-Hold functions, and Euro-spec carbon fiber center console trim. After an outcry from dedicated Audi enthusiasts, the manufacturer decided to bring the wagon version of its vaunted RS6 to the U.S. for the first time during the 2020 model year. It received nearly instant critical acclaim for its aggressive styling, everyday practicality, and outstanding performance. Power comes from a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8, rated at 591 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed automatic transmission.
sections.Equipment: A window sticker is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: Executive Package Black Optic Package Driver Assistance Package 22-inch wheels Sport exhaust Air suspension Head-up display Bang & Olufsen Sound system
sections.Seller Notes: This RS6 is offered with a transferable warranty valid until May 2031 or 100,000 miles, and a tire and wheel protection package valid until May 2027. Documentation regarding the service contract is pictured in the photo gallery. The seller reports that paint protection film has been applied to the entire exterior. The tires on this RS6 carry 2023 date codes.
